title: It is almost never wasabi.
description:
It is almost never wasabi. Most of what is served worldwide, and even much of what is served in Japan, is horseradish and mustard with green colouring standing in for the real plant.

Real wasabi barely tolerates being farmed. It needs a narrow band of cool temperature and constantly flowing clean water, which is why it is grown almost exclusively in specific Japanese mountain regions.

Roughly what a kilogram of real, fresh wasabi can cost, in US dollars. Horseradish grows almost anywhere and costs a fraction of that.

The substitute is also spicier than the real thing.
